title: Why Weddings Cost $34,000 (Say "Wedding," Price Jumps)
alts: The Wedding Markup Is Real. Here's the Proof.
Why the Same Cake Costs More the Moment You Say 'Wedding'
line1: Dave called the same bakery twice for the same cake. Once as a 'party,' once as a 'wedding.' The price jumped. Here's the real math.
summary: Dave and his partner call the same bakery twice for the same cake: once as a 'party,' once as a 'wedding.' The quote jumps. We dig into whether the 'wedding markup' is real (Consumer Reports' secret-shopper test found vendors quoting weddings higher in 28% of calls), what an actual American wedding costs on average in 2026 ($34,200, per The Knot), where that money really goes (venue and catering eat almost half the budget), why the guest list is the single biggest lever in the whole budget, the $66 billion wedding industry, and the debt and regret so many newlyweds report afterward. Then: how to shrink the guest list, get quotes before saying 'wedding,' pick an off-season date, and budget by priority instead of tradition. This is also our 50th episode - a short thank-you to close out the series.
